summary: Session pin split when routing policy updated mid-rollout causes inconsistent canary traffic and 5xxs for tenant
description: Customer reports a spike in 5xxs and inconsistent responses after we adjusted a routing policy mid-canary. Symptoms indicate session tokens were split between the old and new routing path resulting in duplicate canary assignments and model pin conflicts for pinned sessions on Dedicated capacity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer pins model 'redwood-7b-v2' for tenant crimson-analytics on Dedicated pool A.
2) Initiate a weighted canary rollout of 'redwood-7b-q4_0' at 10% via routing policy change (weight-by-header + hash override).
3) During the rollout window, change routing policy to enable header-based sticky affinity (enableSticky=true) without preserving legacy session tokens.
4) Observe that ~8-12% of existing sessions suddenly see a different model than their pin or receive 5xx due to mismatched KV cache token references.
5) Errors are reproducible for requests that include the legacy session cookie (sid=) and the new header (x-tenant-affinity) together.
6) Reverting the policy back to previous config causes some sessions to remain pinned incorrectly until edge cache TTL expires or manual flush is performed.

investigation_notes: Root cause: routing policy toggle enabled a new sticky-affinity path that used header-based tokens instead of preserving the existing session cookie token namespace. The edge proxy created dual records (cookie + header) that mapped to different model variants and the serving runtime did not have logic to reconcile mismatched KV cache namespaces for pinned sessions.

Reproducible path: requests that present both legacy sid cookie and new x-tenant-affinity header follow a code path where router favors header-based affinity but leaves cookie-affinity in edge cache, leading to session-store and serving-runtime seeing different provenance for a session and attempting to load incompatible KV cache shards.

Scope: affected only tenants on Dedicated capacity using session pins and that also change routing policy mid-rollout. We estimate 1 customer impacted in this incident (Crimson Analytics) with brief user-facing errors for ~45 minutes.
Interim mitigations: 1) rollback policy, 2) invalidate edge-affinity cache for the tenant, 3) instruct customer to rotate session cookies if anomalies persist. These reduced errors to baseline.

Permanent fix: preserve legacy token namespace on policy toggles, add reconciliation step in serving-runtime to fallback to pinned KV namespace when detecting token namespace mismatch, add e2e test that mimics legacy cookie + header affinity during canary rollouts.
Related prior incidents: SUP-4721 (canary fallback misroute), SUP-8234 (stale-route-cache during rollout) — similar symptoms but different mechanism.
resolution: Rolled back the routing policy change at 2026-03-10T15:22Z and invalidated the edge affinity cache for tenant crimson-analytics. Coordinated with the customer to rotate session cookies for lingering sessions. Deployed hotfix to routing reconciler on 2026-03-12 that preserves legacy token namespaces when enabling sticky header affinity and added a reconciliation path in serving-runtime to prefer pinned KV namespace on token mismatch. Follow-ups: update canary rollout runbook, add automated integration test that exercises mixed token (cookie+header) cases, and notify account team with postmortem.
